summary: An OpenAI researcher announces GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra, a model that scales parallel test-time compute, claiming it cuts the time to generate a proof for a long-standing problem from about a day to about an hour.

mechanisms.reason: The post describes pushing test-time compute from seconds to weeks, meaning far more compute is spent per query than prior models.
mechanisms.quote: But as we push ttc from seconds to weeks, latency becomes a bottleneck.

mechanisms.reason: Scaling parallel test-time compute to weeks-long reasoning implies sustained state and cache pressure per query, though the post does not state memory figures directly.
mechanisms.quote: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra scales parallel ttc.

mechanisms.reason: A stated large reduction in time-to-solution for a hard, long-standing problem via parallel test-time compute is presented as a step change enabled by the new model.
mechanisms.quote: The time taken to generate a proof to a 50-year-old problem drops from perhaps a whole day to a single hour.

practices.reason: A named new model claims a large latency reduction for long-horizon reasoning tasks via parallel test-time compute scaling, relevant to teams building on reasoning-heavy workloads, but the claim rests on a single unreplicated example.
practices.quote: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra scales parallel ttc. The time taken to generate a proof to a 50-year-old problem drops from perhaps a whole day to a single hour.

notable_reason: A first-party claim of a new model that scales parallel test-time compute to cut latency on research-grade reasoning tasks by roughly 24x is a concrete, quotable capability and infrastructure-demand signal, not routine chatter.
